text: How poor versus rich people buy a house.
Benny finds a four hundred thirty thousand dollar house on Zillow.
He puts five percent down: twenty-one thousand five hundred. All his savings.
The bank lends him the rest. Thirty years. Seven percent.
His payment: about twenty-seven hundred dollars a month.
Over thirty years, he pays almost a million dollars.
More than half of it is just interest. The bank's profit.
Then property taxes. Insurance. A new roof. Benny is house poor.
Now Rick. Same savings. But he buys a fourplex: four homes, one building.
With an FHA loan, he puts just three and a half percent down, and lives in one unit.
He moves into one. And rents out the other three.
Three tenants pay about fifteen fifty each. That covers his whole mortgage.
Rick lives almost free. His tenants pay off his building.
In thirty years, Benny owns one house. Rick owns four, and still collects rent.
Benny worked for his house. Rick's house worked for him.
Would you rather be Benny or Rick? Comment below.
